headline: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue tops the territory, Long Howie takes first loss
lede: Week 6 came in loud at the top and quiet at the bottom, with WeBleedOrangeAndBlue hangin' 132.67 on the board and Scott's Hype scratchin' out 78.33. Four of the 8 races were decided by less than 7 points, which is the kind of week that makes a fella check the wagon wheels twice. No team's unbeaten, no team's winless, and the trail's still crowded.
paragraphs: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue struck the richest vein in the territory, 132.67 to 106.15 over Long Howie, the widest margin of the week at 26.52. The Chiefs defense dug up 28.0 all by itself, and even Kimani Vidal's 4.6 couldn't slow the wagon down. Long Howie got 24.55 from Michael Penix Jr. but started Harold Fannin Jr. for 0.85 while Michael Mayer sat on 9.55, and a better lineup was worth 8.7 more. That drops Long Howie to 5-1 and puts WeBleedOrangeAndBlue at 4-2 with 4 straight.

Jack Attack rode Josh Allen's 22.35 to a 111.15 to 86.68 win over Dart Star Orchestra. The sorriest lineup in the league belonged to Dart Star Orchestra: a better arrangement was worth 28.4 points, and the Browns defense sat on the bench with 18.0 of its own. Christian McCaffrey did his part with 22.65, but T.J. Watt's 1.0 and that parked defense sent Dart Star Orchestra to 1-5 on a 5 game skid.

e-mans revenge took it 99.04 to 88.44 over densmen, with Matthew Stafford throwing in 21.84. densmen actually had the best starter on the field, C.J. Stroud at 29.29, but DJ Moore posted a clean 0.0 and DeVonta Smith's 13.55 never left the bench. That's 3 wins in a row for e-mans revenge at 3-3, and 4 straight losses for densmen at 1-5.

Lowest score of the week met its match: Zihuatanejo squeaked by 85.31 to 78.33 over Scott's Hype, a margin of 6.98. Here's the pretty part: Zihuatanejo left nothing on the table, 0.0 points a better lineup would have added, with Harrison Butker's 12.0 leading the way. Scott's Hype had Travis Hunter and his 16.55 watching from the wagon seat, and a better lineup was worth 14.4 more, which is more than the gap.

Warthogs made it 5 in a row, 114.87 to 109.06 over HAWKSRULE, by a margin of 5.81. Jordan Love paid out 21.52 for the Warthogs, who are 5-1 even with Cade Otton's 0.6 in the lineup. HAWKSRULE got 19.0 out of a kicker, Chris Boswell, and still came up short at 2-4.

Aeil edged Norskes U Betcha 96.5 to 92.52, a margin of 3.98, on the back of Jayden Daniels and his 29.7. Norskes U Betcha had the hottest starter in the game, Trevor Lawrence at 32.47, plus Drake London, who leads all 39 qualifying players in First Read Share at 89% of targets, the alpha stat for who the offense hunts for first. Didn't matter: Tyler Shough's 27.08 sat on the bench, and a better lineup there was worth 11.7.

Justin's Bad Team held off Jrod 116.04 to 112.85, just 3.19 between them. Kenneth Walker III hauled in 28.55 for the winners, who left Kyle Pitts Sr. and his 17.0 on the bench and still found a way; a better lineup would have added 21.0. Jrod got 26.85 from Caleb Williams, but Juwan Johnson's 0.0 at tight end is the kind of hole that swallows a 3.19 margin.

Closest race of the week: sisu 100.01, Super Troopers 97.53, a margin of 2.48. The Steelers defense put up 22.0 for sisu, and Sonny Styles turned in the best defensive day in the league at 11.0. Super Troopers ran a tidy ship, only 1.15 points of better lineup available, but Kaleb Johnson's 0.1 was the difference between 4-2 and 4-2 with a smile.;
sign_off: 7 weeks left before the regular season closes up shop and 8 wagons make the playoff train. Plenty of trail yet, pardners, so keep your lineups honest and your benches lonesome.
purse: The commissioner's purse goes 4 deep this week: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue takes $40 for 132.67, Justin's Bad Team banks $20 for 116.04, Warthogs collect $10 for 114.87, and Jrod rounds out the money with $5 for 112.85. That's 3 weeks in the money now for WeBleedOrangeAndBlue and Jrod both, and 2 apiece for Justin's Bad Team and Warthogs.
